message.content:
A.) Since \(a\mid b\) and \(b\mid 60\), we have \(a\mid 60\). True.

B.) Since \(b\) is a divisor of \(60\), \(60\) is a multiple of \(b\). True.

C.) \(b\) does not have to divide \(c\). For example, let \(a=5\), \(b=10\), and \(c=12\). Then \(a\mid b\), and \(b,c\) are divisors of \(60\), but \(10\nmid 12\). False.

D.) If \(a=20\), then \(b>20\) and \(b<60\). The only divisor of \(60\) strictly between \(20\) and \(60\) is \(30\), but \(20\nmid 30\). So \(a\) cannot be \(20\). True.

E.) If \(b<0\), then because \(a\mid b\), the divisor \(a\) cannot be less than \(b\). So \(a<b\) is impossible. Thus \(b\) cannot be negative. False.

The false statements are C and E.

The answer is C, E.
